items.detail: The **Nasdaq** rose 1.11% to 26,430.89 Monday, and the S&P 500 gained 0.41% to 7,690.73, bouncing back from last week's tech selloff.
items.why: Buyers returned to chipmakers, and the chip index ended an eight-day losing streak, its longest in 18 years.

items.detail: **CoreWeave** fell another 1.5% Monday even as Micron and Nvidia each rose about 2%, so the AI debt worry is still there.
items.why: CoreWeave's roughly $50 billion of debt is still the focus, and big tech earnings are the next test of AI spending.

items.detail: The **10-year Treasury yield** rose to about 5.10% and the 2-year to 4.75%, even though traders now expect the Fed to pause in October.
items.why: Inflation risks keep futures traders betting the Fed will raise rates again by December.

items.detail: South Korea's **Kospi** fell about 2.7% midday Tuesday, wiping out Monday's 1.8% rebound, and SK Hynix headed for its lowest close since April.
items.why: Worries about AI spending hit Korean chipmakers again ahead of big tech earnings.

items.detail: The **Sensex** fell 876 points to 73,852.90 Monday and the Nifty slipped below 23,000 to 22,888.95, with Indian markets closed Tuesday for Dussehra.
items.why: Disappointing Axis Bank results, weaker IT stocks and oil near $108 ended a two-day winning streak.

items.detail: The US **Russell 2000** is still about 11% below its August record of 3,068.42, which keeps it in correction territory.
items.why: About 40% of small companies' debt has floating rates, so 10-year yields near 5.1% hurt them directly.

items.detail: **Bitcoin** slipped back to about $81,500 Tuesday after failing to break $83,000 on Monday.
items.why: Sellers held the $82,000–$83,000 range even as tech stocks rebounded, and greed readings cooled.

items.detail: **Ether** fell 1.1% to about **$2,396**, slipping back below $2,400.
items.why: Ether ETFs lost $320 million last week, putting October outflows near $1 billion.

items.detail: **Solana** held near **$104**, a day before Wednesday's Alpenglow upgrade, which aims to confirm transactions in 150 milliseconds.
items.why: Continued outflows from US Solana ETFs are offsetting hopes for the upgrade, keeping SOL between $100 and $110.

items.detail: **Gold** fell about 0.5% Monday and traded near **$4,138** Tuesday morning, below the $4,150 level it had been testing.
items.why: A firmer dollar and a 5.10% 10-year Treasury yield made non-yielding bullion less attractive.

crossCuttingTheme: The AI-chip rebound looks fragile: US chipmakers bounced Monday but Korean chipmakers fell again Tuesday, while 10-year yields near 5.1% held back gold, small caps and bitcoin.
